correctness.rationale: Dvorkin's classifications give exactly the five normal classes and Lemma 7.4 gives the composition law. All table entries except \(g\star g=g\) and \(h\star g=g\) are formal substitution consequences. On finite S4 frames, Proposition 2.2 identifies \(g=\Diamond\Box\Diamond p\) with accessibility to maximal worlds; the same relation represents the Grz class because \(\Diamond\Box p\equiv\Diamond\Box\Diamond p\). Applying the operator once more to the maximal-cluster relation leaves it unchanged, and adding identity edges before applying it also leaves the maximal-cluster relation unchanged, proving the two remaining products. Finite completeness lifts the identities to the logics. The actual exhaustive small-frame verifier was inspected and agrees with all 25 products, but is corroborative only.

value.rationale: Composition is intrinsic to interpretation theory. The result turns two five-class lists into the complete algebra of iteration, proves the two targets share the same monoid, and shows every parameter-free normal self-translation stabilizes after one iteration. This is a natural structural refinement rather than a renamed classification.
residual_risks: The parameterized setting is much larger and untouched.

final_claim: The five parameter-free normal modal-to-modal translation classes in each of \(\mathsf{S4}\) and \(\mathsf{Grz}\) form the same five-element noncommutative idempotent monoid under composition, with identity represented by \(\Diamond p\) and multiplication table as stated in the record.
limitations: The finite-frame relation for the nontrivial operator is used only through finite completeness; no pointwise representation on arbitrary infinite S4 frames is asserted.
